## About

I am a Ph.D. student in Political Science at the University of Houston, specializing in Public Policy and Research Methods. My research interests include technology and governance, AI governance, policy adoption and implementation, immigration, and gender policy. I am particularly interested in using quantitative and computational methods to examine how political institutions shape policy decisions and outcomes.

## Research

Ibnat, Anika. (2026). “Explaining Cross-National Variation in the Implementation of Policies Addressing Technology-Facilitated Violence Against Women and Girls.” Working paper, University of Houston.

## Teaching

Teaching Assistant | University of Houston (Fall 2025–Present)

Support undergraduate courses in U.S. Government and Political Statistics through grading, course management, student assistance, and instruction in quantitative analysis using R/RStudio.

Teaching Assistant | University of Texas at San Antonio (Fall 2022–Summer 2024)

Assisted with five undergraduate courses through grading, classroom instruction, exam proctoring, student support, and preparation of instructional materials.

Teaching Interests: Public Policy, Political Research Methods, Quantitative Analysis, Comparative Politics, and Technology & Governance.
